headline: A CoSN Era Ends as Ed Tech Confronts the Gap Between AI Policy and Classroom Reality
thesis: EdTech Digest closes the book on Keith Krueger's 32-year run at CoSN the same week EdSurge and Brookings show how unevenly AI and screen-time policy are actually reaching classrooms.
summary: Ed tech's community marks a changing of the guard this week: EdTech Digest bids farewell to Keith Krueger after 32 years leading CoSN, even as ISTE+ASCD names new board leadership heading into its next conference cycle. The transition lands amid mounting evidence that policy is outpacing practice — EdSurge profiles a researcher who spent a year coding AI guidance from more than 100 school districts into a five-level framework, and pairs it with a Gallup/Walton Family Foundation survey finding most teachers have received no formal training on classroom AI at all. Brookings adds an equity lens to the broader screen-time and AI-restriction wave sweeping districts, warning that uniform enforcement can fall hardest on students with disabilities and Black students unless policies are calibrated rather than applied as blanket rules. Interoperability keeps expanding outward: 1EdTech heads to Thessaloniki for Learning Impact Europe and a Latin America assessment webinar, Ed-Fi ships API v8.0, and EDUCAUSE's late-September conference will draw much of the same crowd. On the access and accountability side, Common App's direct-admissions program grows to 234 colleges for the 2026-27 cycle just as Inside Higher Ed reports the U.S. Department of Education is still chasing over a thousand institutions for overdue student-outcomes data — a compliance gap EdTech Magazine's new procurement guide implicitly argues better tooling could help close. The fall conference calendar keeps filling in behind it all, from EdTech Week's October return to Columbia to Ed-Fi's November Alliance Summit.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · September 8, 2026 · Items were sourced and dated via web-search indexing rather than live page fetches this run (direct fetches to source sites were blocked); a few sources (THE Journal, Education Technology Insights, Ed-Fi) had no September-dated coverage surface in search, so their most relevant recent items are listed instead with a note.

themes.title: Teacher Readiness Lags Behind AI's Classroom Arrival
themes.body: A Gallup/Walton Family Foundation survey covered by EdSurge finds most teachers have received no formal guidance on classroom AI use, even as THE Journal's industry-leader predictions push districts toward more deliberate, human-centered rollouts.

themes.title: AI and Screen-Time Policy Collide With Classroom and Equity Realities
themes.body: EdSurge follows a researcher who coded AI policy from over 100 school districts into a five-level framework, while Brookings warns that new screen-time restrictions risk falling unevenly on students by disability and race unless enforcement is calibrated, not uniform.

themes.title: Ed Tech's Leadership Ranks Turn Over
themes.body: EdTech Digest marks Keith Krueger's departure after 32 years leading CoSN, the same week ISTE+ASCD names new board leadership heading into its next conference cycle.

themes.title: Interoperability Agenda Expands Across Borders and Systems
themes.body: 1EdTech's push heads to Thessaloniki for Learning Impact Europe and a Latin America assessment webinar, while Ed-Fi's newly shipped API v8.0 keeps expanding the data standard that EDUCAUSE's late-September conference will also spotlight.

themes.title: Data Shapes the Admissions and Accountability Conversation
themes.body: Common App's direct-admissions program grows to 234 colleges for the 2026-27 cycle as Inside Higher Ed reports most, but not all, institutions have now supplied overdue federal outcomes data, with EdTech Magazine's new procurement guide aiming to streamline the buying process behind it.

themes.title: Fall Conference Calendar Keeps Filling In
themes.body: EdTech Week confirms its October 13-15 return to Teachers College at Columbia, ISTE+ASCD's Edtech Leader Certification enrollment closes September 17, and Ed-Fi's Alliance Summit follows in November.
